nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-02.title: Inclusion-exclusion
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-02.body:
$35-10=25$ students own at least one. Then $25=20+11-x$, so $x=6$.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-02.title: Venn diagram
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-02.body:
If everyone counted twice is removed, $20+11=31$ counts cover $25$ students, so $31-25=6$ students were counted twice, i.e. own both.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-03.title: Use the sides
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-03.body:
With legs $a=BC$, $b=AC$: $\cot A=\frac ba$ and $\cot B=\frac ab$, so the product is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-03.title: Complementary angles
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-03.body:
$B=90^\circ-A$, so $\cot B=\tan A$ and $\cot A\tan A=1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-04.title: Track the water
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-04.body:
The original solution has $0.4\cdot5=2$ quarts of water. After adding $5$ quarts there are $7$ quarts of water in $10$ quarts, i.e. $70\%$.

**Answer: $70\%$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-04.title: Track the acid
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-04.body:
The acid, $3$ quarts, is unchanged and now makes up $\frac{3}{10}=30\%$ of the solution, so water is $70\%$.

**Answer: $70\%$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-06.title: Count factors of 5
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-06.body:
Each trailing zero needs a factor $10=2\cdot5$, and factors of $2$ are plentiful, so count factors of $5$: there are $\lfloor400/5\rfloor=80$ multiples of $5$, $\lfloor400/25\rfloor=16$ multiples of $25$ (an extra factor each), and $\lfloor400/125\rfloor=3$ multiples of $125$ (another extra each); $625>400$. Total $80+16+3=99$.

**Answer: 99**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-07.title: Express in terms of selling price
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-07.body:
If $S$ is the selling price, the profit is $0.2S$ and the cost is $0.8S$. The profit on cost is $\frac{0.2S}{0.8S}=\frac14=25\%$.

**Answer: $25\%$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-10.title: Pythagorean theorem
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-10.body:
Let the radii be $R>r$. The radius of the small circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the chord and bisects it, so $R^2=r^2+6^2$. The area of the ring is $\pi(R^2-r^2)=36\pi$, so $k=36$.

**Answer: 36**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-10.title: Special case
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-10.body:
The answer cannot depend on the radii, so let $r\to0$: then the chord is a diameter of length $12$, $R=6$, and the area is $36\pi$.

**Answer: 36**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-11.title: Count from each vertex
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-11.body:
Each of the $100$ vertices joins to $97$ others by a diagonal (all but itself and its two neighbours). Each diagonal is counted twice, so there are $\frac{100\cdot97}{2}=4850$.

**Answer: 4850**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-11.title: Pairs minus sides
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-11.body:
$\binom{100}{2}=4950$ segments join pairs of vertices; $100$ of them are sides, leaving $4850$ diagonals.

**Answer: 4850**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-12.title: Chain of isosceles triangles
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-12.body:
Let $\angle A=x$. Since $FA=FE$, $\angle FEA=x$ and the exterior angle $\angle EFD=2x$. Since $EF=ED$, $\angle EDF=2x$, and in triangle $ADE$ the exterior angle $\angle DEC=x+2x=3x$. Since $DE=DC$, $\angle DCE=3x$, and in triangle $ADC$ the exterior angle $\angle CDB=x+3x=4x$. Since $CD=CB$, $\angle B=\angle CDB=4x$, and $\angle C=\angle B=4x$. Then $x+4x+4x=180$, so $x=20$.

**Answer: $20^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-13.title: Compare speeds
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-13.body:
His speed is $\frac{70}{2.5}=28$ mph. The new time is $2.5-0.75=1.75$ hours, requiring $\frac{70}{1.75}=40$ mph, an increase of $12$ mph.

**Answer: 12 mph**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-14.title: Factor
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-14.body:
$2^x+2^{x-1}=2\cdot2^{x-1}+2^{x-1}=3\cdot2^{x-1}=48$, so $2^{x-1}=16=2^4$ and $x=5$. Since $2^x+2^{x-1}$ is increasing, this is the only solution.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-14.title: Guess and check
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-14.body:
Try $x=5$: $32+16=48$. The left side is strictly increasing in $x$, so $x=5$ is the only solution.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-15.title: Use the LCM
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-15.body:
Leaving remainder $1$ on division by $2$, $3$ and $4$ means $n-1$ is a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(2,3,4)=12$: $n=13,25,37,\ldots$ (and $n=1$, which is not a multiple of $5$). The first multiple of $5$ is $25$.

**Answer: 25**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-15.title: List multiples of 5
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-15.body:
Check the multiples of $5$ in order: $5$ leaves remainder $2$ on division by $3$; $10$ and $20$ are even; $15$ is divisible by $3$; $25=24+1$ leaves remainder $1$ on division by $2$, $3$ and $4$.

**Answer: 25**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-16.title: Factor
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-16.body:
The two numbers $1$ and $\sqrt2$ have sum $1+\sqrt2$ and product $\sqrt2$, so the equation is $(x-1)(x-\sqrt2)=0$, with roots $x=1$ and $x=\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $1$ and $\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-16.title: Check a root
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-16.body:
$x=1$ gives $1-1-\sqrt2+\sqrt2=0$. The product of the roots is $\sqrt2$, so the other root is $\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $1$ and $\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-17.title: Pick a volume
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-17.body:
$11$ units of water become $12$ units of ice. Melting $12$ units of ice gives back $11$ units, a loss of $1$ out of $12$, i.e. $\frac1{12}$ of its volume.

**Answer: $\frac1{12}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-19.title: Positions of the hands
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-19.body:
Measured from 12, the minute hand is at $20\cdot6^\circ=120^\circ$ and the hour hand at $7\cdot30^\circ+20\cdot0.5^\circ=220^\circ$. The angle is $100^\circ$.

**Answer: $100^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-19.title: Count hour marks
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-19.body:
There are $30^\circ$ between numerals. At 7:20 the minute hand is on the 4 and the hour hand has moved $\frac13$ of the way from 7 to 8. The angle is $3\cdot30^\circ+10^\circ=100^\circ$.

**Answer: $100^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-20.title: Two isosceles triangles
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-20.body:
Since $DQ\parallel BC$, $\angle DQB=\angle QBC=\angle DBQ$, so triangle $DBQ$ is isosceles and $DQ=DB=8$. Similarly, with $CQ$ bisecting the exterior angle at $C$, $\angle EQC$ equals the alternate angle between $CQ$ and line $BC$, which equals $\angle ECQ$; so $EQ=EC=6$. The points lie in the order $D,E,Q$ on the line, hence $ED=DQ-EQ=8-6=2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-21.title: Multiply
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-21.body:
There are $4$ houses, $4$ floors each, $4$ apartments per floor, $4$ doors per apartment and $4$ hinges per door: $4^5=1024$ hinges in all. (If 'the house' is read as a single house, the count is $4^4=256$; the league accepted both answers.)

**Answer: 1024**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-22.title: Total gain
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-22.body:
In $24$ hours the clock gains $24\cdot5=120$ seconds $=2$ minutes, so the correct time is $5{:}58-2$ minutes $=5{:}56$.

**Answer: 5:56**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-23.title: Use a common unit
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-23.body:
Let there be $18$ green stickers. Then there are $3$ red and $1$ blue, $22$ in all, and green is $\frac{18}{22}=\frac{9}{11}$.

**Answer: $\frac9{11}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-23.title: Algebra
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-23.body:
With $R$ red stickers, green $=6R$ and blue $=\frac R3$, total $\frac{22R}{3}$. Green fraction $=\frac{6R}{22R/3}=\frac{9}{11}$.

**Answer: $\frac9{11}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-24.title: Split the area
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-24.body:
The altitude from $A$ to $BC$ is $\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$, so the area is $60$. Triangles $APB$ and $APC$ fill triangle $ABC$: $\frac12\cdot13\cdot PX+\frac12\cdot13\cdot PY=60$, so $PX+PY=\frac{120}{13}$. (The ratio $2:3$ is not needed.)

**Answer: $\frac{120}{13}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-25.title: Equation
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-25.body:
If the cost is $C$ cents, $C=\frac34C+15$, so $\frac C4=15$ and $C=60$ cents.

**Answer: 60 cents**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-25.title: Think in quarters
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-25.body:
The extra $15$ cents is the missing $\frac14$ of the price, so the price is $4\cdot15=60$ cents.

**Answer: 60 cents**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-27.title: Equation
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-27.body:
Twice half of $x$ is $x$, so $\frac x3+x=\frac{4x}{3}=36$ and $x=27$.

**Answer: 27**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-28.title: Drop the altitude
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-28.body:
Let $BC=6y$ and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, so $BM=3y$ and $EM=y$. Then $AM^2=17^2-9y^2=15^2-y^2$, so $8y^2=64$, $y=2\sqrt2$, and $BC=12\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $12\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-30.title: Solve for sine and cosine
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-30.body:
Squaring, $1+2\sin x\cos x=\frac1{25}$, so $\sin x\cos x=-\frac{12}{25}$. Then $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ are the roots of $t^2-\frac15t-\frac{12}{25}=0$, namely $\frac45$ and $-\frac35$. In the second quadrant $\sin x=\frac45$, $\cos x=-\frac35$, so $\tan x=-\frac43$.

**Answer: $-\frac43$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-30.title: Tangent half-angle identity
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniorb-30.body:
From $\sin2x=-\frac{24}{25}$ and $\sin2x=\frac{2\tan x}{1+\tan^2x}$: $12\tan^2x+25\tan x+12=0$, so $\tan x=-\frac34$ or $-\frac43$. $\tan x=-\frac34$ gives $\sin x=\frac35,\cos x=-\frac45$, whose sum is $-\frac15$, so it is extraneous. Hence $\tan x=-\frac43$.

**Answer: $-\frac43$**
